title: driver.v2: what an engine driver declares, takes and gives back
description: The engine driver contract, version 2. A driver is the core's own code for one engine; this file freezes the data that crosses between a driver and the rest of the core, so that every engine lane builds the same thing. The record at the root is the driver's DECLARATION: the engine's name and one true-or-false flag for each thing the engine can do. The calls are: start(session, workspace, env) -> handle; send(input); interrupt(turn_id); resume(engine_session_id) -> handle; fork(engine_session_id, at) -> engine_session_id; parse(line) -> event drafts. A call whose flag is false is refused 'unsupported' BEFORE any side effect: no process is started, no byte is written to the engine, no record is made. Which flag each call needs: a second send of a user_message to the same worker needs multi_turn; a send of a user_message while a turn is in progress needs mid_turn_input; a send of an approval_answer needs permission_bridge; interrupt needs interrupt; resume needs resume; fork needs fork. typed_limits says the driver reads limits from typed fields of the engine's stream (never from text); usage says it reads token counts. start, the first send, close and parse need no flag. The one-turn path that exists today (one prompt, standard input closed, read until the result) is a driver whose flags are all false.

driver.description: The contract version the driver implements.

flags.description: Every flag is always present. mid_turn_input is true only when multi_turn is true: input in the middle of a turn needs a worker that keeps its input open.

start.description: What start is given. The environment is not in this record: it is built by the child-environment policy and handed over separately, and it never appears in a record.

engine_session_id.description: null for a new conversation. A string resumes that conversation, and needs the resume flag.

handle.description: What start and resume give back: the run the worker lives in, and the engine's own id for the conversation once the engine has reported one.

input.description: What send takes. user_message: one input of a turn. approval_answer: the core's answer to the engine's own permission request, sent only by the approval queue through its private binding. close: end the worker's input; the engine finishes and exits.

fork.description: What fork takes: the conversation to copy, and the turn to copy it at (null for its latest state). It gives back the new conversation's engine_session_id.

refusal.description: How a call whose flag is false is refused. Nothing happened before this answer.

event_draft.description: What parse gives back for one line of the engine's output: zero or more of these. A draft is an event before the core has numbered and timed it; its payload is exactly the payload of that type in event.v1. A driver may draft only these types. It never drafts an approval request: it asks the approval queue, and the core writes the event.
